title: One row per log attribute
prompt: The logging team wants to know which attributes each record carries. Write `solve(application_logs_raw)` so it returns one row per attribute of each good record: `log_id` and `attribute` (the key's name).
rules: Only lines that are JSON objects count; skip the rest.
Each key of a record's `attributes` gives one row. A record with no `attributes`, or an empty one, gives no rows.
Keep repeated records: a record shipped twice gives its rows twice.
Return `log_id` and `attribute`, both text, in that order.
hints: First get the good records with a `parse` function and `flatMap`, as in the lesson.
A second `flatMap` can turn one record into a list of `(log_id, key)` pairs.
`rec.get("attributes") or {}` gives an empty dict when the field is missing or null, so the record gives no pairs.
starter:
